problem.title: Sulfur ion orbit after acceleration through 1 kV (JEE Advanced type)
problem.text:
A singly charged sulfur ion (mass 32 u) starts from rest, is accelerated through a
potential difference of 1000 V, and then enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.50 T
directed perpendicular to its velocity. The accelerating voltage gives it a speed of
7.7655e4 m/s. What is the radius of the circular orbit it follows in the field?
problem.source: Problem type after the JEE Advanced alpha/sulfur ion-ratio question (dataset: JEEBench, dair-iitd/jeebench, gold ratio 4); statement rewritten, posed for one ion at a time, not reproduced.

trajectory.integrator: RK4 (exact for constant acceleration; <0.5% phase error on cyclotron orbits at the sampled dt)

because.detail: A charge with mass, free to move. Both a field source and the thing that responds to a field — which is precisely why the field -> force -> trajectory chain needs no special case.
A region of stated uniform magnetic flux density.
The surrounding medium and fields. Defaults are an idealised vacuum with no gravity, which is what textbook electrostatics problems assume -- stated here as an editable value instead of a footnote.

because.law_label: Circular motion in a uniform magnetic field
because.law_statement: A charge moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field travels a circle whose radius is mv/(qB) and whose period is independent of speed.
